content:
Hi all, I wanted to share something new a few of us are building. I wasn't sure where to post this, but it is aimed at people interested in mathematics research and using AI to help accelerate research, so I figured this was good.

I'm with Talmenta, a startup co-founded by Jasper van de Kreeke (some of you may know him from his work in homological mirror symmetry / AI for math). To be clear, we are not a theorem-proving model or benchmark. What we do is build research management and collaboration tooling with AI support throughout it all. We're built to help people who are interested in research in the AI-for-math space.

So, since there are a fair amount of researchers in this channel, I wanted to ask: for those of you running or part of a research group in this space, what are the main issues when it comes to managing projects, collaborators, or day-to-day workflows? I'm curious about whether tooling like this would actually help, and I would love to hear any thoughts you might have, whether you have suggestions, love the idea, you're interested in learning more, or think it's a horrible idea.

Reply here or DM me if you'd rather chat directly.
